videos.description:

En este vídeo repasamos los cambios que realmente merece la pena conocer, qué aportan en el día a día y cuáles pueden marcar una diferencia práctica en accesibilidad.
Si usas iPhone con VoiceOver, entra y descubre qué cambia para ti.

videos.title: Yo ya no persigo las noticias: ahora vienen a buscarme
videos.description:
En este vídeo les presento cMRSS, una aplicación accesible que permite reunir en un mismo lugar las fuentes de noticias y contenidos que realmente nos
interesan.
Podemos añadir medios y páginas mediante sus fuentes RSS, organizar lo que seguimos y consultar las novedades sin tener que ir saltando de una web a otra.
Pero hay una función que a mí me ha gustado especialmente: también podemos añadir canales de YouTube y seguir sus nuevas publicaciones desde la propia
aplicación, sin necesidad de entrar continuamente en YouTube para comprobar qué han publicado.
cMRSS no es gratuita, y eso también hay que decirlo. Pero después de usarla y comprobar lo que me ofrece, en mi caso considero que merece la pena la inversión.
En el vídeo les enseño cómo funciona, qué posibilidades ofrece y por qué se ha ganado un sitio entre las aplicaciones que utilizo para mantenerme informado.

videos.title: TifloAcosta ya tiene app: todo cambia a partir de aquí
videos.description:
TIFLOACOSTA APP — ACCESO DIRECTO
Este enlace abre directamente TifloAcosta App. No necesitas descargar ningún archivo ni registrarte para entrar. Desde ahí puedes utilizar la aplicación en el navegador y, si quieres, instalarla en tu dispositivo para tenerla disponible como una app más.
TifloAcosta da hoy uno de los pasos más importantes desde que comenzó este proyecto.
Durante mucho tiempo hemos ido creando vídeos, cursos, guías, documentos, recursos en español y en inglés y una comunidad que sigue creciendo. El problema es que todo ese material estaba repartido entre distintos lugares.
Ha llegado el momento de empezar a reunirlo.
TifloAcosta ya tiene su propia app.
Desde ella puedes buscar recursos por palabras, recorrerlos por categorías, consultar las novedades, guardar tus favoritos y acceder al catálogo completo de vídeos del Canal TifloAcosta.
Además, la aplicación se ha pensado desde el principio teniendo en cuenta la accesibilidad y el uso con lectores de pantalla.
En este vídeo te enseño cómo funciona, qué puedes encontrar dentro y cómo puedes instalarla para tener TifloAcosta mucho más cerca.
La demostración práctica se realiza en iPhone utilizando VoiceOver, y también explico cómo acceder e instalarla desde Android y Windows.
Si quieres entrar directamente mientras ves el vídeo, este es nuevamente el enlace:
La aplicación seguirá creciendo.
Iremos incorporando nuevos recursos, mejorando lo que ya existe y ajustando aquello que la experiencia real de los usuarios nos vaya indicando.
Porque esto no pretende ser simplemente otra página donde acumular enlaces.
La idea es mucho más ambiciosa: crear un lugar estable, accesible y sencillo desde el que entrar a todo lo que TifloAcosta va construyendo.
Hasta ahora, TifloAcosta era principalmente un canal, una comunidad y una colección de contenidos repartidos por distintos espacios.
Desde hoy empieza a tener su propia casa.
Y acabamos de abrir la puerta.

videos.title: Este atajo no pregunta, ve un código y se pone a investigar
videos.description:
Ponle un código delante… y a ver qué pasa
Hoy les traigo uno de esos atajos que empiezas haciendo para resolver una cosa y al final termina haciendo bastante más de lo previsto.
La idea es sencilla: encontrar un código y averiguar qué contiene.
Puede trabajar con códigos que estén en una imagen o una captura guardada en el iPhone, pero también con códigos que tengamos delante y podamos captar con la cámara.
Y no nos quedamos únicamente con los códigos QR.
El atajo también puede reconocer códigos de barras y, cuando encuentra información que merece la pena investigar, utiliza Internet para intentar averiguar qué hay detrás de ese código y ofrecernos información útil.
Por ejemplo, podemos encontrarnos un código de barras en un producto y querer saber qué es, o recibir una imagen que contiene un QR sin tener otro teléfono disponible para escanearlo.
La intención ha sido precisamente esa: tener una herramienta sencilla y accesible que podamos lanzar desde el iPhone y dejar que haga el trabajo.
En el vídeo les enseño cómo funciona y las distintas posibilidades que ofrece.
IMPORTANTE:
Para utilizar este atajo es necesario tener instalada la aplicación gratuita Actions, ya que algunas de las funciones que utiliza el atajo proceden de esta aplicación.
Descargar Actions desde la App Store:
Instalar el atajo:
Una vez instalada Actions, conviene abrirla al menos una vez. Si sus acciones no aparecen posteriormente en la aplicación Atajos, reinicien el iPhone.
Como siempre, este atajo lo comparto para que puedan probarlo, jugar con él y, sobre todo, sacarle partido.

videos.title: VoiceOver: ¿Esa voz es nueva?
videos.description:
VoiceOver no tiene por qué quedarse únicamente con las voces que trae el iPhone.
En este vídeo pruebo dos formas de ampliar su repertorio: las voces de Visionauta, una aplicación de reconocimiento del entorno que permite incorporarlas al sistema, y Runa TTS, una nueva plataforma que todavía se encuentra en fase beta y no está disponible en la App Store.
Escucharemos cómo suenan y qué posibilidades ofrecen para darle a VoiceOver un registro diferente.

videos.title: Un ciego prevenido vale por dos: alertas sísmicas en el móvil
videos.description:
En este vídeo hablo de algo que ojalá no tengamos que necesitar nunca, pero que conviene conocer: cómo puede ayudarnos el móvil a recibir avisos relacionados con terremotos.
Primero explico qué opciones existen en Android y en iPhone para recibir alertas en tiempo real cuando hay un terremoto cerca, siempre dependiendo del país, la cobertura y los sistemas oficiales disponibles.
Después presento una aplicación llamada Earthquake, disponible para iPhone y Android, que permite hacer seguimiento de movimientos sísmicos, consultar información sobre terremotos, avisos de tsunami y otros datos útiles. La app se puede usar con VoiceOver y puede resultar interesante para quienes quieran estar informados desde el móvil de forma accesible.
No se trata de vivir con miedo, sino de saber qué herramientas tenemos a mano cuando la tierra decide moverse sin pedir permiso.

videos.title: zEdit: por fin editar vídeo y audio con VoiceOver deja de ser una tortura
videos.description:
En este vídeo te presento zEdit, una aplicación para iPhone que permite editar archivos de vídeo y audio de forma accesible usando VoiceOver.
Con zEdit puedes recortar vídeos, cortar partes que no necesitas, unir varios clips, extraer el audio de un vídeo, añadir audio, silenciar sonido, ajustar volumen, trabajar con grabaciones y exportar el resultado final para guardarlo o compartirlo.
Lo más importante es que todas estas funciones están pensadas para poder usarse con VoiceOver. Los botones, controles y opciones de la app permiten que una persona ciega o con baja visión pueda manejar la edición multimedia con mayor independencia.
zEdit puede resultar útil para quienes crean contenido para YouTube, redes sociales, podcasts, mensajes de audio o cualquier trabajo donde sea necesario preparar, modificar o ajustar archivos multimedia desde el iPhone.
Una app sencilla, práctica y accesible que intenta resolver uno de los grandes problemas que seguimos encontrando las personas ciegas: editar vídeo y audio sin depender siempre de herramientas visuales o de la ayuda de otra persona.
videos.excerpt: En este vídeo te presento zEdit, una aplicación para iPhone que permite editar archivos de vídeo y audio de forma accesible usando VoiceOver.

videos.title: SonarPad: la app accesible que lo quiere hacer todo
videos.description:
Hoy te presento SonarPad, una app accesible que reúne muchas herramientas útiles en un solo lugar.
Con SonarPad puedes leer documentos, libros y otros contenidos de forma cómoda. También puedes buscar información en Wikipedia, mantenerte al día con las noticias, escuchar cualquier emisora de raio, escuchar los podcast que quieras, convertir archivos multimedia, consultar el tiempo, revisar tu calendario, crear rutas accesibles y descubrir próximos estrenos de cine con sus tráileres.
Todo desde una aplicación pensada para facilitar el acceso a la información, la lectura, la orientación y el entretenimiento.
SonarPad no es solo una app más. Es una herramienta con muchas posibilidades para personas ciegas y con baja visión que buscan soluciones prácticas, accesibles y fáciles de usar.
Lectura, noticias, documentos, multimedia, rutas, calendario, tiempo, cine y mucho más en una sola app: SonarPad.

videos.title: ¿Y si hablar otro idioma dejara de ser un muro?
videos.description:
Google Traductor ha incorporado una función de traducción en tiempo real que permite mantener conversaciones de una forma mucho más natural entre personas que hablan idiomas diferentes.
En este vídeo muestro cómo se activa en el iPhone, cómo funciona y qué posibilidades abre en situaciones cotidianas: viajes, consultas rápidas, conversaciones con personas de otros países, práctica de idiomas o momentos en los que necesitas entender y responder sin estar copiando y pegando frases.
No sustituye a un intérprete profesional cuando hay temas delicados, pero sí puede convertirse en una herramienta muy útil para el día a día.
Una función sencilla, accesible y con mucho más potencial del que parece a primera vista.

videos.title: Tu iPhone habla al cargar: crea un sonido automático al conectar y quitar el cargador
videos.description:
En este vídeo te muestro paso a paso cómo crear una automatización en el iPhone para que suene un aviso personalizado cuando conectamos el cargador y también cuando lo retiramos.
La idea es sencilla: usar la app Atajos para que el iPhone reproduzca un archivo de sonido en dos momentos concretos, al iniciar la carga y al dejar de cargar. Es una función muy útil para cualquier persona que quiera personalizar su iPhone, pero especialmente práctica para quienes usamos VoiceOver y necesitamos confirmaciones claras sin depender de la vista.
Durante el vídeo se ve todo el proceso: cómo crear la automatización, cómo elegir la condición relacionada con el cargador, cómo indicar el archivo de sonido que queremos reproducir y cómo dejarlo funcionando correctamente.
Una pequeña personalización que convierte una acción tan simple como enchufar el iPhone en algo más cómodo, claro y hasta un poco divertido. Porque ya que vivimos rodeados de cables, cargadores y avisos por todas partes, al menos que el móvil avise como uno quiere.

Muy atentos: Después de casi dos años de desarrollo, por fin llega TCA ConvertDoc 1.5. No es una simple actualización: es un salto generacional con las funcionalidades que me habéis ido pidiendo en los comentarios del blog, sobre todo desde la entrada de la versión 1.4. Para quienes aún no lo conozcan: ¿Qué es TCA ConvertDoc? TCA ConvertDoc es una pequeña utilidad portable y gratuita para Windows, con interfaz 100% accesible y atajos de teclado, que nos permite convertir entre multitud de formatos de documentos (doc, docx, RTF, epub, pdf, HTML, odt, txt, markdown, PNG, JPG, PPTx), hacer OCR a imágenes y PDFs, y ahora, además, traducir. Y todo, de forma individual o por lotes (carpeta entera de una sola vez). Pues bien, la 1.5 llega cargada de novedades. Os las cuento todas. Novedades de TCA ConvertDoc 1.5 1. Conversión DOCX → PDF (individual y por lotes) Ahora podéis convertir documentos de Word a PDF con un solo clic. ¿Tenéis una carpeta llena de? docx? La conversión masiva procesa todo el directorio de golpe, manteniendo el formato, las imágenes y la estructura del documento. Perfecto para preparar entregas, archivar o compartir. 2. Conversión PPTX → Markdown (individual y por lotes) Algunos me preguntasteis en la entrada de la 1.4 por qué ciertas presentaciones de PowerPoint no se pueden leer con lectores de pantalla. Pues esta es una de las soluciones: extrae el contenido de tus presentaciones a Markdown limpio y editable, ideal para documentación, blogs, wikis o migrar contenido. También funciona en lote para carpetas completas. 3. PDF escaneado PDF buscable (OCR) "¿Se puede convertir un pdf en un pdf con capacidad de búsqueda?" — me preguntasteis en los comentarios de la 1.4. ¡Ahora sí! Añades un PDF que es solo imagen (un escaneo sin capa de texto), TCA ConvertDoc le aplica OCR y te devuelve un PDF con texto seleccionable y buscable. Accesibilidad real para documentos heredados, del tipo que sea. 4. JPG / PNG PDF buscable Construye PDFs accesibles a partir de imágenes sueltas. Cada imagen pasa por OCR y se une en un único PDF donde puedes buscar, copiar y seleccionar el texto. Ideal para digitalizar notas, facturas, páginas de libros o documentos fotografiados con el móvil. 5. Traducción integrada! (¡la gran novedad!) Llevaba muchísimo tiempo queriendo incorporarle la traducción a TCA ConvertDoc, y por fin está aquí. Ahora el programa es capaz de traducir archivos completos a cualquier idioma usando dos motores: • Argos Translate | Offline | Descarga previa de los paquetes de idioma (privacidad total, sin internet) • Google Translate | Online | Conexión a internet, máxima calidad Formatos soportados: .txt, .docx y .pdf. Y lo mejor de todo: traduce incluso archivos grandes como libros enteros. El motor procesa el texto en fragmentos inteligentes, mantiene la estructura del documento (párrafos, saltos de página, estilos en DOCX) y te entrega el archivo traducido listo para usar. Nada de copiar y pegar por trozos, ni de chocar con límites ridículos de caracteres. Un detalle importante sobre Argos: la primera vez que uses Argos con un idioma, te aparecerá un diálogo ofreciéndote descargar los paquetes de ese idioma... y solo esa única vez. A partir de ahí, ese idioma queda instalado en el programa y funciona totalmente sin conexión. Tranquilo, no te lo volverá a pedir. 6. Selector de idiomas del OCR (Tesseract) completo En la 1.4 teníamos 3 idiomas de OCR (español, inglés e italiano). Ahora, en el cuadro combinado de idioma del OCR aparecen todos los idiomas que soporta Tesseract. Ya no hay que editar configs a mano ni adivinar códigos: eliges el idioma y listo. 7. Arreglos y optimizaciones internas OCR de archivos grandes: se ha reescrito el proceso para manejar PDFs e imágenes de gran tamaño sin agotar la memoria ni bloquear la interfaz. Gestión de hilos optimizada en las conversiones por lotes. Mejor detección de orientación y enderezado automático en imágenes escaneadas. Logs más claros y barra de progreso real en las operaciones largas. Y muchas otras mejoras internas que hacen el programa más estable y rápido. Requisitos para utilizar TCA ConvertDoc 1.5: • Windows10 (x64) en adelante. • portable, sin instalación. • Para Argos: el programa te ofrece descargar los paquetes del idioma la primera vez que lo uses (un solo diálogo), y luego funciona offline • Para Google Translate: conexión a internet Tip: si vas a trabajar mucho con traducción offline, entra a Argos, descarga de una vez los idiomas que más uses (español, inglés, francés, alemán, chino, japonés, árabe...) y olvídate. Luego todo irá 100% sin conexión. Tutorial: 📘 TCA ConvertDoc 1.5: OCR en PDF, 🚀 traduce libros y más! Si trabajas con documentos, investigas, digitalizas archivo o necesitas mover contenido entre idiomas, esta versión te va a ahorrar horas. Muy atentos, porque hoy les traigo una variante muy especial: TCA-MediaDownloader versión 2.9a, una variante totalmente funcional a agosto de 2026, que descarga, pre-reproduce y, sobre todo, que no sufre los problemas que arrastran otras versiones y otros programas! ¿Qué pasa con las demás versiones y programas? Seguramente ya lo han vivido: hay programas que no descargan, otros que si descargan el archivo queda sin sonido, o que directamente lanzan errores al intentar reproducir. Y esto no es un problema exclusivo de estas versiones ni de estos programas. La causa real son los constantes cambios que realiza YouTube y otras plataformas, que modifican su funcionamiento con frecuencia para dificultar las descargas externas. Por ese motivo, la librería yt-dlp debe estar constantemente adaptándose a dichos cambios, lanzando parches que a veces llegan antes y a veces llegan tarde, y esos cambios rompen muchas funciones hasta que llega la solución. Esta variante 2.9a está optimizada justamente para ese escenario, y en las pruebas que realicé (y las personas que me ayudaron a probarla) funciona sin problemas de reproducción ni de descarga. Si con esta versión no te descarga o reproduce un contenido, difícilmente lo podrás hacer con otro programa. Así de simple. TCA-MediaDownloader 2.9a puede reproducir y descargar lo que otros programas no pueden. Novedades importantes de TCA-MediaDownloader 2.9a Elección de la rama de yt-dlp Ahora, dentro de las opciones, podemos elegir la rama de actualización de yt-dlp que queramos utilizar: • Estable (recomendada): la versión probada y oficial. • Nightly (desarrollo): aquí llegan antes los cambios y los parches ante las modificaciones de las plataformas. Puede ser algo más inestable, pero cuando hay muchos cambios de por medio es la que antes reacciona. Yo personalmente la tengo configurada en la rama de desarrollo y me va bastante bien, pero cada uno puede dejar la que prefiera. Nueva categoría: Cookies Las opciones ahora incluyen una nueva categoría llamada Cookies, donde, de forma opcional, podremos añadir un archivo .txt que contenga nuestras cookies. ¿Para qué sirven? Algunos sitios web requieren que hayas iniciado sesión para descargar ciertos contenidos. Con las cookies, el programa se autenticará igual que lo hace tu navegador. Puedes exportar tus cookies desde el navegador usando una extensión como Get cookies.txt LOCALLY (disponible para Chrome y Firefox) y seleccionar aquí el archivo .txt generado. En el tutorial muestro el paso a paso completo: Recuerda: esta opción no es obligatoria para que el programa funcione, pero sí es recomendable tenerla activada como una capa más para que las descargas no fallen. Correcciones varias en el código. Se han corregido varias cosas, como mejora de la identificación del PC, guardado correcto de las opciones, nueva dependencia para mejorar descargas y muchas correcciones menores. Para la comunidad de personas con discapacidad visual, contar con herramientas que permitan descargar y gestionar este contenido de forma autónoma es vital. news.title: Apple Releases iOS 27 and iPadOS 27
news.summary: iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 are now available to the public. This post contains Apple's Release Notes for iOS 27, as well as links to all of AppleVis' content related to these updates. Also included are instructions on how to install the update. iOS 27 Release Notes iOS 27 introduces the next generation of Apple Intelligence and Siri AI, as well as new features to help parents create safe digital experiences for kids, and improvements that make iOS more responsive and delightful to use. Siri AI is an entirely new version of Siri that is more intelligent, knowledgeable, and capable. The next generation of Apple Intelligence also powers new features across apps that simplify the things you do every day, like editing images in Photos, communicating in Messages and Mail, and browsing in Safari. New parental controls and significant updates to Screen Time make it more intuitive and easy to use, so parents can feel confident that they're building the right digital experience for their child. And with improvements that span design, performance, connectivity, search, and more, the experience on iOS 27 has been refined and elevated, so it feels even better to use. Siri AI (All iPhone 16 models and later, iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max) A more capable and conversational version of Siri is rolling out to users. It helps you find what you need and get more done, drawing on capabilities like personal context understanding, app actions, onscreen awareness, and access to broad world knowledge. New voice experience offers more expressive and natural-sounding voices, and lets you customize expressivity and pace to make Siri more personal to you using powerful on-device models on iPhone Air and iPhone 17 Pro models and later. Dedicated Siri app provides an easy way to revisit an existing conversation or kick off a new one, and privately syncs conversations across your Apple products with iCloud. Siri mode in Camera integrates Visual Intelligence into the Camera app, letting you ask questions and take action with what's in front of you, like splitting a bill or looking up nutritional info for a plate of food. Write with Siri enables you to generate a draft from scratch, edit what you've written, or get feedback from Siri virtually anywhere you type. In Messages & Mail, Siri personalizes your writing style based on your relationships, and uses unique phrases and punctuation that you've previously used in your conversations with those people. Apple Intelligence across apps (All iPhone 16 models and later, iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max) Photos. Spatial Reframing lets you adjust the composition of a photo after it was taken by virtually changing the camera position. Extend tool intelligently expands images beyond their edges with realistic infill, so you can straighten horizons, change aspect ratios, or add more space around a subject. Clean Up supports removing even larger objects, with more realistic, high-quality results, and you can choose between Fast mode for small blemishes or High Quality for more intricate edits. Safari. Organize by Topic uses Apple Intelligence to sort your tabs, analyzing webpages and automatically grouping similar tabs together. Notify Me can periodically check a webpage for updates, like price changes and item availability. Describe an Extension lets you create a custom extension using natural language to adjust your view of a website's content or formatting. All-new Image Playground uses a new generative model to make high-quality images in virtually any style, including photorealistic, lets you modify your images using touch and natural language, and lets you generate Lock Screen wallpapers and Contact Posters with personalized suggestions. Describe a Shortcut lets you use natural language to create a shortcut or refine an existing one. Home. Summarized activity notifications combine related alerts across accessories into a single notification. Video descriptions for HomeKit Secure Video recordings summarize what's happening in a clip for eligible iCloud+ subscribers. Camera clip search lets you find specific moments from your HomeKit Secure Video cameras by searching in the Home app or Spotlight when on an eligible iCloud+ plan. Describe an event in Calendar lets you use natural language to create an event, and details like the time, location, invitees, and event title are filled in using Apple Intelligence. Suggestions in Mail help you take action based on the context of your emails, like getting directions to a restaurant you booked. Call Context in the Phone app understands when you're speaking to certain businesses and proactively surfaces relevant information from across your apps, like a confirmation code or a reservation number. Accessibility. VoiceOver enhancements include more detailed and contextual image understanding for photos, charts, and screenshots, a conversational experience that lets you ask questions about your screen or surroundings, and a new way to get answers fast with an Action button integration. An enhanced Magnifier experience offers conversational visual assistance for users with low vision, with a high-contrast interface and natural language app controls for zooming and other Magnifier functions. A smarter Accessibility Reader uses intelligence to provide better text cleanup and formatting, images and tables, on-demand summaries, and translation. Voice Control flexible inputs help you navigate your device with just your voice by describing elements on screen in your own words, like "tap the gear" or "tap the button in the top right". And more, including additional ways to create and modify Genmoji, automatic proofreading, and more accurate dictation using an on-device model on iPhone Air and iPhone 17 Pro models and later. Child Safety Improved setup experience for new child accounts lets parents choose the exact apps their kids can access when they set up an iPhone for their child. Ask to Browse gives parents the option to approve each new website before their child can view it. Expanded Communication Safety protections help intervene before children see gore or violent content in shared images and videos. Time Allowances help parents set boundaries around how long kids can use apps across Entertainment, Games, and Social Media apps, offering guidance based on expert research and tailored to each child's age. Schedules let parents choose which apps their kids can access at different points in their day and across weekdays and weekends. Redesigned Screen Time settings give parents at-a-glance information about how their kids use their devices, and controls to adjust access in just a few taps. System Improvements Liquid Glass refinements improve overall readability, and a new slider in Settings lets you personalize its appearance from ultra-clear to fully tinted . Faster performance in experiences across the system, including app launches, new photos loading in your Photos library, and AirDrop transfers. Improved search provides more relevant and comprehensive results in Spotlight, Photos, and Mail. Connectivity Assist enables more seamless transitions between Wi-Fi and cellular networks. And more improvements across apps and experiences, including enhancements to iCloud Shared Albums in Photos, Custom EQ for AirPods, support for perimenopause and menopause in Cycle Tracking in the Health app, and independent volume settings for Alarms and Timers. news.title: macOS Golden Gate: New Features, Changes, Improvements, and Bugs for Blind and Low Vision Users
news.summary: Apple has today released macOS 27 Golden Gate to the public. As usual, we won’t cover the mainstream features here, concentrating instead on what's new and changed for blind, DeafBlind, and low vision users. For an overview of the mainstream changes, we recommend this in-depth review by MacStories . Please remember to check the section about bugs to see if now is the right time to upgrade. There’s no harm in holding off a few weeks or months to let Apple address a problem you may find too disruptive to deal with. A note to braille users: the AppleVis team members doing testing with macOS Golden Gate are not heavy braille users. We have no information as to how well braille works in this release, so please keep this in mind when upgrading. If you are a braille user who has experience with Golden Gate, please share your findings in the comments to help the community. Changes for VoiceOver and Braille Users Improved Image and Screen Descriptions As on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, VoiceOver in macOS Golden Gate can use Apple Intelligence to describe and answer questions about images or the current screen as it appears visually. Focusing on an image and pressing VO-Shift-L will describe the image, and you can find additional options, such as the ability to ask about an image, explore the image spatially, or describe the current screen, by pressing VO-Shift-R from anywhere in macOS. For added convenience, commands in this menu can be mapped in VoiceOver Utility > Commands. Note that while VoiceOver can describe and answer questions about what's on the screen, it cannot directly interact with elements like VOCR or Screen Recognition on iOS and iPadOS can. New Verbosity Options for Coding With macOS Golden Gate, you can customize how information such as line numbers, errors, and warnings are reported by VoiceOver in code editors like Xcode. These settings can be found in the new "Coding" tab in VoiceOver Utility > Verbosity. We do not currently know which code editors besides Xcode respect these settings. New "Actions" rotor for trackpad users With macOS Golden Gate, you can perform custom actions for the focused element, the same actions available in VoiceOver's Actions menu, using trackpad commands. To do this, enable trackpad commands if they're not already enabled, turn the rotor to "Actions," swipe up or down with one finger to select a custom action, and double-tap to activate it. "Ducking Amount" setting The "Ducking Amount" setting for determining how much other audio is ducked when VoiceOver is speaking, originally introduced with iOS 18 and iPadOS 18, has been brought to macOS with the release of Golden Gate. It can be found in VoiceOver Utility > Sound. Braille Improvements While it is not something we have been able to test, we are aware of the following improvements for braille users in macOS Golden Gate: As on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, text field labels can now be shown in braille. You can change the format these labels are presented in, or hide them entirely, by going to VoiceOver Utility > Braille > Layout, and clicking Text Field Labels. As on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, Braille Access in macOS Golden Gate supports plain text (txt) and portable document format (PDF) files. Improvements for Low Vision Users While it is not something we have been able to test, we are aware of the following improvement for low vision users: As on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, content in Accessibility Reader can now be summarized and translated while retaining its original formatting on macOS Golden Gate. If you are a low vision Mac user, we would love to hear in the comments your experience and thoughts on this and any additional enhancements you encounter in macOS Golden Gate. Other Changes As on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, the Aaron (English US), Arthur (English UK), Catherine (English Australia), Gordon (English Australia), and Martha (English UK) voices have been reintroduced with macOS Golden Gate. Like other voices, they can be used with Siri, as well as for accessibility functions like VoiceOver and Read & Speak. As on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, subtitles for spoken dialog in videos where captioning is not already provided can be generated automatically in macOS Golden Gate. These can be turned on and adjusted when playing a video by clicking the "show legible media selection menu" button in the playback controls group. Writing Tools, previously accessed from many apps' Edit menus, as well as many text fields' context menus, is now accessed with VoiceOver by focusing on a text field and choosing "Show Writing Tools" from the Actions Menu. When toggling Cursor Tracking with VO-F3, its state is reflected in the "Mouse pointer:" popup menu in VoiceOver Utility. In prior versions of macOS, the state of Cursor Tracking was not reflected in this popup menu, which had the potential to confuse users. Change List In its support documentation, Apple lists the following changes for VoiceOver users in macOS Golden Gate: You can now turn off announcements that webpages send automatically, such as live scores, new messages, or status updates. Turn off Enable Web Announcements to silence announcements from a single area of a webpage or from the entire page. VoiceOver remembers your choice for that website, so the area stays silent the next time you visit. With the new Coding tab in the Verbosity category of VoiceOver Utility, you can choose whether VoiceOver announces line numbers, and whether it plays a tone or speaks a description when it encounters an error, a breakpoint, or the program counter. Bug Fixes and New Bugs for VoiceOver Users Below are lists of the bugs we believe to have been resolved in macOS Golden Gate, as well as new bugs introduced in this release. We strongly recommend that you read through the list of new bugs and any replies before updating, as this will allow you to make an informed decision on whether to install macOS Golden Gate or wait for a future release. While we are confident in the status of issues contained in this post, we do not claim that our bug list is definitive or that our assessments are infallible. Some issues may manifest only under specific conditions; this is all the more likely as software continues to add more features, and the number of available configurations and use cases in Apple's ecosystem continues to grow. You likely will not experience every bug that we list, and it is also likely that you will encounter issues that we did not experience during our own testing and daily use of macOS Golden Gate. To ensure the information here is as complete and accurate as possible, we would appreciate input from those who have installed macOS Golden Gate. Please confirm if you are encountering the same problems listed or if you have found workarounds. Please also let us know about any additional issues not mentioned here. Of course, it's even more important that you report any new bugs directly to Apple - they're already aware of the ones listed here. For an explanation of why and how to report bugs to Apple, see this post. Accessibility Bugs Resolved in macOS Golden Gate To the best of our knowledge, Apple does not routinely publish lists of bug fixes for VoiceOver or Braille across releases; thus, it is difficult to get a complete accounting of every issue that has been resolved or what fixes users can expect to see upon upgrading to macOS Golden Gate. With this in mind, our testing suggests that the following issues present in macOS Tahoe have been resolved or meaningfully improved in macOS Golden Gate: VoiceOver no longer speaks list items on webpages unreliably. Pauses between sentences are no longer extended when using VoiceOver's "Say All" command. It is once again possible to reply to a message in the Message app by selecting the "Reply" action in the Actions menu. The Actions menu for Messages in the Messages app no longer contains redundant tapback actions. New Bugs for VoiceOver Users in macOS Golden Gate Our testing suggests that the following bugs have been introduced in macOS Golden Gate: After clicking the “Proofread” button in the Writing Tools popover using VoiceOver, only the Next, Previous, and Close buttons are visible, with no way to view the specific changes made to the text. There is no way to open or redownload apps from the “Apps & Purchases” page in the App Store using VoiceOver, with each app conveyed only as a button with no actions available and nothing to interact with besides the app’s name. To redownload a previously purchased app, you must click the [app name] button to open the product page, and then click the "Redownload" button in the toolbar. The sections and buttons in Safari’s Page Menu lack accessibility labels. Interacting with a section and pressing VO-Space on an item (all of which are clearly labeled) works to activate the item; however, interacting with each item in a section reveals an unlabeled button. When playing audio or video, VoiceOver announces “system has new window” once the media has started playing. The identity and purpose of this window is not clear from this announcement, and no new items appear in the application or window chooser menus. Other Possible Bugs In addition to the bugs listed here, we strongly recommend you read this Megathread about the macOS Golden Gate RC , , as it contains a wealth of community reports about and experiences with the Release Candidate version of the software that may differ from our own. macOS Golden Gate release notes macOS 27 introduces Siri AI powered by Apple Intelligence, new parental controls, and an expansive set of improvements that make your Mac even more responsive, reliable, and delightful. Experience the new Siri AI Introducing Siri AI, an entirely new version of Siri powered by Apple Intelligence that’s more personal, more capable, and more conversational. It is integrated into Spotlight, so you can search for answers about almost any topic right from where you already search for things across your system. It can draw on personal context to find things across your messages, mail, photos, and more. And it can get things done across your apps, just by asking. Revisit and resume past conversations in the new dedicated Siri app, synced with iCloud across your Apple devices. Siri AI is rolling out to users, and you can get started by turning it on in Settings. Take action on what’s onscreen With Visual Intelligence, you can select a window of your screen and Siri can answer questions or take action with what’s onscreen, like adding events to your calendar. You can access Visual Intelligence with a dedicated keyboard shortcut — Command-Shift-Space. Powerful new ways to edit photos Use intelligent photo editing tools to reframe a photo after it’s been taken with Spatial Reframing or expand your shot with the Extend tool. And enhancements to Clean Up let you remove distractions with better quality and more realistic infill, even when the scene is complex. New tools to browse in Safari Automatically group your tabs into topics, so related pages are easier to find. With Notify Me, Safari can monitor pages for changes like price drops or restocks and alert you when it’s time to act. Describe an Extension lets you use natural language to create custom extensions, like adding a button to save your favorite recipes. Easily create Shortcuts using natural language With Describe a Shortcut, you can automate daily tasks with a simple description and all of the required steps are assembled on your behalf. For example, you can describe a shortcut to automatically text your partner when you’re headed home from work with an estimated arrival time based on traffic. Even more refined design Updates to Liquid Glass improve readability, and a new slider lets you customize how it looks, from ultra-clear to fully tinted. Uniform toolbars, edge-to-edge sidebars, and more detailed app icons further elevate the design. New child safety features Powerful new parental controls help parents manage what content their children see, who they can communicate with, and when they can access apps. Ask to Browse requires kids to request permission before visiting any new website in Safari. Communication Safety expands its protections to help keep conversations safe. Time Allowances gives parents more flexible ways to manage kids’ time in apps across categories. Schedules manage which apps kids can access at different times of day and throughout the week. A more responsive and delightful experience An expansive set of improvements make your Mac even faster, more reliable, and easier to use. Better search in Spotlight and Mail helps you find what you’re looking for with greater ease. AirDrop Transfers and network file browsing happen faster. And many more improvements make your day-to-day use more enjoyable. Learn more Discover even more powerful capabilities in the next release by visiting apple.com/os/macos . For information on the security content of Apple software updates, please visit: support.apple.com/100100 . Some features may not be available in all regions or on all Apple devices. To learn more, please visit: apple.com/macos/feature-availability . Usage limits may apply for some Apple Intelligence features. To learn more, please visit: apple.com/apple-intelligence . Software updates, like this one, add new features and improvements that may affect performance and battery life. To learn more, please visit: support.apple.com/125039 . In Conclusion We would like to thank everyone in our community who contributed to AppleVis' testing and bug-reporting efforts during the macOS Golden Gate beta cycle - be it through our Community Bug Program or just by posting on our Forum. Our information about this release is more complete because of you, and we are very grateful to all who took the time to contribute. We'd love to hear your thoughts after you've had a chance to install the upgrade. What new features do you find most useful? Are there any changes you don't like? Please share your feedback in the comments below. When doing so, we ask that you please keep the discussion focused on accessibility issues specifically introduced or fixed in macOS Golden Gate. Our release posts tend to be widely read and garner many helpful responses, so it is all the more important that readers can easily find relevant information. Also, please remember that upgrade decisions are personal, with each user's situation unique - there is no right or wrong choice. Comments criticizing others' decisions are not constructive and do nothing to add to the discussion; but they do set a negative tone and get in the way of readers finding helpful information. Furthermore, not experiencing an issue yourself does not mean that it doesn't exist for others, as bugs can be configuration-specific. Stating that an issue doesn't exist simply because you haven't encountered it is unhelpful. Our aim with these posts is to provide a forum for respectful, constructive, and honest sharing of experiences that inform decisions and empower people. In closing, we thank Apple's Accessibility team for their prompt response in fixing many of the bugs reported during the macOS Golden Gate beta cycle. However, many longstanding issues remain unresolved, and we find the inability to fully use the Proofread function, a key feature of Apple Intelligence, during a cycle where enhancements to Apple Intelligence were heavily emphasized, incredibly disappointing. We encourage Apple to promptly address this and other outstanding accessibility issues discussed in this post and the comments below so that macOS can be as accessible, usable, and enjoyable as possible for all users. To install macOS Golden Gate, choose System Settings from the Apple menu, select General in the table, click Software Update in the scroll area, and click the Upgrade Now button to begin the upgrade process. If other updates are available, you can click the Info button to see details about them and select specific updates to install. More information on how to update the software on your Mac is available on this Apple Support page.

news.title: watchOS 27: A Summary of VoiceOver Features, Issues, and Improvements
news.summary: Apple has today released watchOS 27 to the public. watchOS 27 is compatible with the Apple Watch Series 9 and later and the Apple Watch Ultra 2 and later. Due to the inherent challenges of beta software testing on watchOS, our testing of watchOS 27 has been quite limited. That said, for VoiceOver users, there is at least one new bug that we are aware of and a handful of new features and improvements. New VoiceOver Bugs in watchOS 27 There is rather significant latency with VoiceOver speech when swiping through the user interface. Specifically, there is a delay between when the VoiceOver sound effects/haptics play, and when VoiceOver speaks. Our testing suggests that this issue is not synthesizer-specific. It is unclear to us whether this behavior is simply a function of the newer operating system encountering the limits of hardware (something that has historically been a challenge on Apple Watch devices), or whether this is something that can be resolved by Apple in a future software update. A Feedback report has been filed, and we will keep the community advised as additional information becomes available. If you identify any additional vision accessibility bugs in watchOS 27, please let us know by posting a comment. New VoiceOver Features and Improvements in watchOS 27 There is a new "Tap to Wake" toggle in VoiceOver settings. By default, the setting is enabled, and the Watch will be woken when you tap on the screen. Our best understanding is that disabling this feature should prevent the device from waking when the screen is tapped. It is now possible to customize the speaking of VoiceOver hints in watchOS. Available options are 'Always', 'Never', and 'App-Specific Hints'. On the Clock Face, VoiceOver now speaks the names of Complications before speaking their content. For example, VoiceOver might say, "Weather, Mostly Sunny 65 Degrees," instead of just saying "Mostly Sunny 65 Degrees." For braille display users, there is a new setting, "Translate After a Delay." There are other braille settings that we also believe may be new in this release, but our braille-related testing in watchOS is very limited and so this is not something we are able to comment on with any level of certainty. If you spot any other new features/changes in watchOS 27 or have any corrections to the above, please do let us know by posting a comment. watchOS 27 Release Notes watchOS 27 features the next generation of Apple Intelligence and Siri AI, updates to Workout Buddy, a new tap gesture, a dynamic app grid to make it easier to access your most used apps, and improvements that make watchOS 27 more responsive and delightful to use. Siri AI is an entirely new version of Siri that is more intelligent, knowledgeable, and capable. With improvements that span areas like fitness, design, performance, and more, the experience on watchOS 27 has been refined and elevated, so it feels even better to use. Siri AI A more capable and conversational version of Siri is rolling out to users. It helps you find what you need and get more done, drawing on capabilities like personal context understanding, app actions, onscreen awareness, and access to broad world knowledge. New voice experience offers more expressive and natural-sounding voices, and lets you customize expressivity and pace to make Siri more personal to you using powerful on-device models on paired iPhone Air and iPhone 17 Pro models and later. Dedicated Siri app provides an easy way to revisit an existing conversation or kick off a new one, and privately syncs conversations across your Apple products with iCloud. Apple Intelligence across apps Workout Buddy delivers motivation with new insights and is now available without your iPhone nearby when you have a Wi-Fi or cellular connection. Call Context in the Phone app understands when you’re speaking to certain businesses and proactively surfaces relevant information from across your apps, like a confirmation code or a reservation number. Cycle Tracking Cycle deviation notifications that are suggestive of perimenopause can be received by those age 40 and over. Watch Faces Siri Modular face features a rectangular complication that mirrors the top widget of the Smart Stack, which dynamically updates to show the most relevant widget, as well as a Siri complication to quickly invoke Siri. Smart Stack Single-handed tap gesture enables you to tap your index finger and thumb together once to select a widget in the Smart Stack, even if your other hand is occupied. New suggestion widgets will be surfaced when most relevant to you, including a Parked Car location, birthday reminders for a close contact, balance changes on a transit card, Noise app after a loud noise notification, and more. System Improvements Dynamic app grid highlights your most popular and recently used apps. Find My app is now consolidated into one app to show People, Devices, and Items with a map-centric interface. Media playback now starts faster. Workout app makes distance calculations during treadmill workouts even more accurate from the first step of every walk or run. Fitness app features more accurate route maps after workouts. Battery extension notifications may be proactively offered to disable certain features to increase battery life, including gestures, Start Workout reminders, and Raise to Speak method of invoking Siri. Shazam in the Smart Stack and Music Recognition app identifies songs offline without an internet connection and delivers results automatically when you’re back online. Liquid Glass refinements improve readability with more uniform refraction and improved contrast. For information on the security content of Apple software updates, please visit: https://support.apple.com/100100 Usage limits may apply for some Apple Intelligence features. To learn more, please visit: https://www.apple.com/apple-intelligence Software updates, like this one, add new features and improvements that may affect performance and/or battery life. To learn more, please visit: https://support.apple.com/125039 How to Update watchOS 27 is available via Over-the-Air Update (Settings > General > Software Update) or by going to the Watch app on your iPhone and navigating to General > Software Update. To install the update, your Watch must be connected to its charger and have at least 50% battery power.

news.title: iOS 27 and iPadOS 27: A Summary of VoiceOver and Braille Issues and Improvements
news.summary: iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 were released to the public on Monday, September 14, 2026. This post contains a summary of new bugs and fixes impacting VoiceOver and Braille support that the AppleVis Editorial Team has independently validated during our use and testing of these releases. The information contained in this post is compiled from our own use and testing of iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 during the beta period from June to September 2026; as well as from validated reports submitted by others through our Community Bug Program and shared on the AppleVis Forum. Our sincere appreciation goes to everyone who so generously took the time to share their findings with us. At the outset, we need to state explicitly that the bug list contained in this post is not definitive and that our assessments are not infallible. While we are confident in the presence of the issues discussed in this post, there are many other reports shared on the AppleVis Forum by members of our community that we have not been able to independently replicate with the available information. Many of these reports represented use cases that are different from those of our team; and a small number were issues that, despite understanding how to reproduce them, we did not get the same results. We say all of this so that readers understand the limits of our own testing, and that others' experiences may be different from ours. An issue not being present in our bug list does not mean the issue does not exist; it simply means that we are either unaware of or unable to reproduce it. As is our routine practice, each bug in this post has been given a severity rating. These ratings are based upon what we believe to be the implications for accessing and using features and functionality for the average user; the level of impact on the overall user experience; and whether or not there is an effective workaround for the issue. However, as these ratings are subjective to an extent, it is very possible that they may not reflect your own opinion or use case. With this in mind, we strongly recommend reading this full post and any replies before updating to iOS 27 and iPadOS 27; as we believe this will help you make an informed decision on whether to install the software at the current time or to wait for a future release. We also strongly recommend that you read this Megathread about the iOS 27 RC , as it contains a wealth of community reports about and experiences with the Release Candidate version of the software. Some issues listed in this post and on the Forum may manifest only under specific conditions; this is all the more likely as software continues to add more features and the number of devices, available configurations, and use cases in Apple's ecosystem continues to grow. You likely will not experience every bug that we list, and you likely will not agree with every severity rating for the bugs that you do experience. While we wish it were otherwise, this is to be expected. And as is the nature with all software, it is also likely that you will encounter issues that are not reported in this post. To ensure the information in this post is as complete and accurate as possible, we would appreciate input from those who have installed iOS 27 or iPadOS 27. Please confirm if you are encountering the same problems listed or if you have found workarounds. Please also let us know about any additional issues not mentioned here. Of course, it is even more important that you report any new bugs directly to Apple - they are already aware of the ones listed in this post. For an explanation of why and how to report bugs to Apple, see this post. With all of the preamble out of the way, below are the new bugs for VoiceOver and Braille users which members of the AppleVis Editorial Team have personally experienced and believe to be present in iOS 27 and iPadOS 27: A Major Change to VoiceOver's Audio Profile In iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, there is a significant change in the sound profile of VoiceOver when the device's internal speaker is used. When compared to iOS 26, VoiceOver audio in iOS 27 has significantly less bass, particularly at lower volume levels. The resulting sound might best be described as 'neutral' or 'flat', with significantly less of the low-end emphasis and other processing that has characterized VoiceOver audio in recent versions of iOS/iPadOS. If you have not yet upgraded to iOS 27, we believe that you can get a reasonable approximation of how VoiceOver will sound on your device by making a phone call, putting the call on speaker, and then using VoiceOver to navigate around the screen; as the flatter, more neutral sound profile that VoiceOver uses during a phone call sounds very similar to what we are hearing in iOS 27. At the time of publication, we do not know whether the change to VoiceOver's sound profile is expected behavior; thus, we are not including it in our bug list. Nevertheless, we feel that users should be aware of this change before upgrading. If we receive additional information, we will update this post accordingly. Serious Bugs When the state of an item changes or the screen updates, VoiceOver does not always recognize/speak the information. This issue has many manifestations, including (but not limited to): When waking the device, VoiceOver may speak the time the device was last woken rather than the current time; When information updates onscreen (such as the status of an operation in an app), VoiceOver may not speak it right away and instead speak the previously displayed text. There is no known workaround, though VoiceOver will eventually speak the updated information if focus is moved off of and back onto the impacted element enough times. The VoiceOver Per-Voice Equalizer (a feature that allows one to customize certain frequency/tonal characteristics of a voice) does not work. There is no known workaround. If you rely on the per-voice Equalizer, we recommend that you do not install iOS/iPadOS 27 until this issue is resolved. The VoiceOver Pronunciation Dictionary does not work reliably, with custom pronunciations often not being obeyed by VoiceOver. There is no known workaround. If you rely on the Pronunciation Dictionary, we recommend that you do not install iOS/iPadOS 27 until this issue is resolved. On some devices, Sound Curtain and Touch Curtain do not work. For affected users, it is possible to partially work around the issue with Sound Curtain by setting the device volume to 0%. There is no known workaround for Touch Curtain. If you rely on Sound Curtain or Touch Curtain, we recommend that you do not install iOS/iPadOS 27 until this issue is resolved. If an external audio device is connected, VoiceOver speech does not work when playing audio in Safari. Pausing the audio causes it to start working again. Sometimes, when reading text, VoiceOver stops speaking and does not resume on its own. This issue does not occur all of the time. When it does occur, speech will stop mid-sentence (and sometimes even mid-word). Touching the screen or performing a touch gesture (like a one-finger swipe left or right) restores speech, and the user can then refocus VoiceOver on the impacted element. In iOS 27's new Recovery Menu, there is no spoken feedback in Diagnostics Mode, rendering this option completely inaccessible. There is no known workaround to make Diagnostics Mode itself usable. If you do manage to accidentally get your device into Diagnostics Mode, our experience is that the device will restart into normal operation after approximately five to ten minutes of inactivity. Moderate Bugs In Safari, the buttons to switch between the Start Page, Reading List, History, and Bookmarks do not work. It is possible to select these buttons, and VoiceOver indicates they have been selected, but the content itself does not update, meaning content cannot be reached. As a workaround, perform a one-finger triple-tap (what is known as a "long press") on the desired button to activate it. Our thanks to AppleVis user Brian Giles for this workaround. When VoiceOver focus is placed inside a text field, and then subsequently moved onto a combo box, the menu automatically opens. On occasions, when swiping through the Lock Screen using one-finger swipe right or left, VoiceOver focus may be inconsistent. When navigating through the Lock Screen using a one-finger swipe right, after the "Swipe up to Unlock" element, the expected behavior is that VoiceOver will focus on the first notification (if present); Focus status (if present); or the first item on the screen, like Flashlight or Camera. However, sometimes, VoiceOver users may find that focus is instead placed on items from the Status Bar, such as Cellular Carrier, Battery Percentage, or the Clock. If VoiceOver focus does land on items from the Status Bar when swiping, it is sometimes possible to continue swiping to the right and get to the first Lock Screen item; however, other times, VoiceOver focus can become stuck in a loop between the time, the "Swipe Up to Unlock" element, Cellular Carrier, an element with no spoken or audible feedback, or any combination of the above. Sometimes, VoiceOver does not speak the time when the device is woken with the Side Button. If this issue occurs, single-tap the screen with one finger to wake the device. After prompting Siri with the Side button, revealing the interface at the top of the screen, nothing happens when double-tapping the "Open in App" button. Double-tapping this button should work to activate it, opening the conversation in the Siri app. In the Phone App, the buttons to switch between 'All' and 'Missed' do not work. This issue can be worked around by either switching to Unified View or swiping through all calls in Classic View. Sometimes, it is not possible to access notifications with VoiceOver that are visually displayed onscreen. Typically, the 'Show notifications' button is present, but on these intermittent occasions, selecting it fails to reveal the notifications, and does nothing. If this issue occurs, double-tap and hold on the "Show Notifications" button, and swipe up. This will reveal the notifications. VoiceOver's 'Copy Speech' function copies the full semantic markup and hints, instead of just the spoken text. For example, in iOS 27, Copy Speech might paste "Latest news, heading Level 2". In previous versions of iOS, Copy Speech would only paste "Latest news," which is the desired behavior. Screen Recognition does not appear in VoiceOver's Quick Settings panel, even if selected for inclusion. The Camera App contains extraneous elements for editing Camera Controls when Edit Mode is not active. This includes "Remove" elements next to each camera control and a "Done" button that does nothing when tapped. When an app is open and VoiceOver focus is placed on the battery indicator, it is not possible to swipe to other items on the status bar. The Direct Touch option in the VoiceOver Quick Settings panel does not work. Minor Bugs In Notification Center, the Rotor Action for clearing all notifications does not work. As a workaround, Locate and double-tap on the "Clear, Notification Center" button, then double-tap on the "Confirm Clear, Notification Center" button that appears. Our thanks to AppleVis Community member Sieghard Weitzel for this workaround. On the Keypad in the Phone app, the button to place the call is labeled as "Call Answer." When focusing on a conversation in the Siri app, the Actions rotor for the conversation contains two identical "Delete" actions. When the device is set to 24-Hour Time, VoiceOver does not correctly speak the time on the top of the hour. When customising VoiceOver touch gestures and you select to replace the current command with a new one, the old command is sometimes not overwritten, necessitating manual removal and replacement. When the Safari toolbar is set to 'Bottom', the "Show Bookmarks" button is incorrectly labelled as "Bookmark." When the VoiceOver cursor reaches the first or last element onscreen in the Camera app, focus loops instead of stopping at the boundary. Improvements for VoiceOver and Braille in iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 To the best of our knowledge, Apple does not routinely publish lists of bug fixes for VoiceOver or braille across releases; thus, it is difficult to get a complete accounting of every issue that has been resolved or what fixes users can expect to see upon upgrading to iOS 27 or iPadOS 27. With this in mind, our testing suggests that the following issues present in iOS/iPadOS 26 have been resolved or meaningfully improved in iOS 27 and iPadOS 27: Stability of VoiceOver focus has been significantly improved across the operating system. The screen no longer locks while VoiceOver is reading a notification on the Lock Screen. Keyboard sounds once again play when VoiceOver is on, regardless of the audio ducking setting. VoiceOver focus is no longer erratic in the App Switcher when it is opened from the Home Screen. The default volume of the Eloquence speech synthesizer more closely matches that of other voices. In Conclusion Our team has compiled lists of new vision accessibility bugs for every major iOS and iPadOS release since iOS 7 in 2013. No software from any manufacturer is completely free of bugs. That said, the number of bugs - particularly those classified as "serious" and involving core VoiceOver and braille functionality - in iOS/iPadOS 27 is deeply concerning. We call on Apple to urgently prioritize fixing the bugs listed in this post, as well as those on The AppleVis Bug Tracker . If you have not already upgraded to iOS 27 or iPadOS 27, we would strongly recommend that you take a few moments to read through any replies to this post before doing so; in case other users' experiences differ from our own. Also, consider that historically, Apple has delivered fixes for many accessibility bugs within the first few x.x.1 updates following major releases, and waiting briefly may allow Apple to resolve any initial problems reported after the public release. In the event that you do encounter an issue that is particularly bothersome, there are some troubleshooting steps you can take. Sometimes, simply toggling VoiceOver off and on again or restarting your device can resolve some issues that may arise following an OS update. Therefore, we highly recommend including these steps as part of your standard troubleshooting process. If restarting VoiceOver and/or your device does not resolve the issue, it might be worth considering a reset of your VoiceOver Settings; to do this, navigate to Settings> Accessibility> VoiceOver> Reset VoiceOver Settings. While this approach requires manually reconfiguring your customized VoiceOver settings, we have heard of multiple instances where a VoiceOver settings reset resolved issues since this feature became available in last year's iOS 26. This suggests that occasionally, problems can be attributed to local factors rather than being OS bugs. Finally, when commenting below, we ask that you please keep the discussion focused on accessibility issues specifically introduced or fixed in iOS 27 and iPadOS 27. Our release posts tend to be widely read and garner many helpful responses, so it is all the more important that readers can easily find relevant information. Also, please remember that upgrade decisions are personal, with each user's situation unique - there is no right or wrong choice. Comments criticizing others' decisions are not constructive and do nothing to add to the discussion; but they do set a negative tone and get in the way of readers finding helpful information. Furthermore, not experiencing an issue yourself does not mean that it doesn't exist for others, as bugs can be configuration-specific. Stating that an issue doesn't exist simply because you haven't encountered it is unhelpful. Our aim with these posts is to provide a forum for respectful, constructive, and honest sharing of experiences that inform decisions and empower people. In closing, we would like to again thank everyone in our community who contributed to AppleVis' testing and bug-reporting efforts during the iOS/iPadOS 27 beta cycle - be it through our Community Bug Program or just by posting on our Forum. Our information about this release is more complete because of you, and we are very grateful to all who took the time to contribute.
